scenes.headline: How one TPU program runs a whole Kimi K3 step
scenes.sub: A megakernel, cross-layer prefetch and a speculative verify.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cardamom! Inferact runs Kimi K3's whole decoder as one TPU program. Here's how it works.

scenes.text: At one user, decoding is a weight read. A megakernel issues each load as early as on-chip memory allows, even across layers, so HBM stays busy.
scenes.mark: as early as on-chip memory allows
scenes.say: At one user, decoding is mostly reading weights. A megakernel starts each load as early as memory allows, even across layers.

left.title: Per-op kernels
items: Each op loads only its own weights
HBM idles through routers and collectives
A ramp and a drain at every boundary
left.say: One kernel per op means memory idles through every router, collective and drain.

right.title: One megakernel
items: Loads start when VMEM has room
Next layer streams in during the experts
right.say: One megakernel starts loads whenever memory has room, so the next layer streams in during this one's experts.

scenes.title: One TensorCore, one job per unit

steps.say: Weights live in HBM. Asynchronous copies move them into VMEM, and they stay until overwritten.
The scalar core runs the layer loop, and turns the router's chosen experts into copy addresses.
The matrix unit does the matmuls; the vector unit does routing, norms and the recurrence.
Even the collectives are inside: hand-written reductions over remote copies.
Inferact's timeline: layer N runs attention, router, shared expert, routed experts, then communicates.
Layer N plus one's attention weights arrive during the routed experts, before they're needed.

items.say: A small drafter proposes seven tokens.
The megakernel verifies eight rows at once, touching far more experts, so the step roughly doubles.
It keeps the agreed prefix, plus one token of its own.

scenes.label: per eight-row verify on 16 TPU v7 chips
scenes.note: 709 tok/s is this step with acceptance forced to 6
scenes.say: A verify step takes about eight and a half milliseconds. The headline is six tokens over that, six forced by a flag.

scenes.title: Batch 1 tokens a second: published vs ceiling
scenes.note: Ceilings: bytes per token over 16 chips' bandwidth
scenes.say: By bytes per token, the GPUs have the higher ceiling. The TPU wins on software: a third of its ceiling, against an eighth.

scenes.text: Issue every weight load as early as memory allows. Here the kernel, not the chip, made the difference.
scenes.say: Issue every load as early as memory allows. Here the kernel, not the chip, made the difference.

recap: One program streams every layer's weights
Headline equals step time times six
scenes.say: One program, loads across layers, and a headline that is a step time times six.
